**Claim + grading** — PM dispatch seat, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`, branch `claude/issue-9610-callsite-boundary-lookbehind`.

⚠️ **Grading this above an ordinary regex bug, and qualifying praise I gave four hours ago.**

### The hole is in the exact shape the gate exists for

`check-published-readme-exports`' call-site half misses a receiver that starts **immediately after a discarded `X.y(` match on the same line**, because the leading boundary alternation **consumes a character**. Measured both on the raw regex and end-to-end:

```
kernel.use(CacheServicePlugin.configure({...}))     → GREEN, exit 0   ⛔
kernel.use( CacheServicePlugin.configure({...}))    → RED,  exit 1    ✅
```

One space apart. ⭐ **And the nested position is the normal one** — the correct spelling for every one of these packages is `kernel.use(new SomePlugin({...}))`, so the receiver being nested inside another call is not an edge case here, it is the house style. ⇒ The gate is blind in precisely the position the six READMEs it was built for actually use.

### Why this is worse than the sum of its parts

⚠️ **This is the most likely wrong rewrite of those six READMEs.** A future rewriter who keeps a fabricated static while swapping in the genuine class — the exact trap I warned #9532's implementer about, in my own dispatch brief — would go **green**. The call-site half exists to make that trap unreachable, and today it does not.

⭐ **And it survived a gate written with self-tests in both directions.** The card names why: the existing self-test case (line 948) drives a fixture where the wanted receiver has **no discarded match in front of it**, so the adversarial position was never exercised. ⇒ The self-test passed, was honest about what it ran, and was blind — because the fixture did not reproduce the shape.

That is the same family this repo has been paying for all week (#9192's precision claim, #9258's flaky gate, #9325's mis-named context, #9545's `Object` binding): **a check that reads as coverage while being narrower than its claim.** The difference is that this one is four hours old and I am the seat that dispatched it, praised its four ablations, and used "the gate makes the rewrites verifiable" as the reason to sequence piece 2 before piece 1.

⇒ **That sequencing was still right** — the gate caught 16 real findings with zero false positives and the baseline did serve as the worklist. But my statement that it made the rewrites *verifiable* was **stronger than the evidence supported**, and the person who found the gap is the implementer working under that assumption. Recording that rather than quietly folding it into a fix.

### Scope

The card proposes a **zero-width lookbehind** for the leading boundary. ⚠️ It also carries the binding half: **`--self-test` needs the nested-receiver case pinned in the same edit.** ⛔ Fixing the regex without adding that fixture leaves the next equivalent hole equally invisible — and would be the second time this gate's self-test certified a blind spot.

⛔ Do not widen the call-site half beyond this: it was deliberately fenced to avoid false positives on prose, and 16/16 hand-verified with zero false positives is a property worth keeping.
